title: Origin of the first human beings
competency: Compare the creationist and the scientific theory, and name early human fossils found in Ethiopia.

keywords.def: A person who believes that God created human beings and the whole universe.
A gradual process of change over a very long time.
The species that human beings belong to.

en.text: There are two theories about where human beings came from. Creationist theory says God created human beings. Scientific, or evolution, theory says humans are the result of gradual, natural change over millions of years. Charles Darwin explained evolution.

screens.title: How did we begin?
screens.ask: How many main theories about the origin of human beings does the book give?
screens.after: The book gives two: the creationist theory and the scientific (evolution) theory.

screens.title: 2.1.2 Origin of the first human beings
paras: There are two theories about the origin of human beings.
They are the creationist theory and the scientific (evolution) theory.

screens.title: The two theories
table: Human beings were created by God. Creationists believe God created humans and the whole universe.
Humans and other living things are the result of gradual, natural changes over millions of years.
screens.note: Charles Darwin (1809–1882) explained the evolutionary process.

en.text: Hominids were the ancestors of human beings. Humans belong to the species Homo sapiens. Australopithecines, or southern apes, were the earliest human species. The fossil of Australopithecus afarensis, called Lucy or Dinkinesh, was found in 1974 at Hadar in Afar, Ethiopia.

screens.title: A famous find
screens.ask: Where was the famous fossil "Lucy" (Dinkinesh) found?
screens.after: Lucy was found in 1974 at Hadar, in the Afar region of Ethiopia.

screens.title: Hominids
paras: Hominids were the ancestors of human beings.
Human beings belong to the species called Homo sapiens.
Australopithecines (southern apes) were the earliest human species. They appeared in Africa about 6 million years ago.
Their fossils were found in Ethiopia, Kenya, South Africa and Chad.

screens.title: Lucy (Dinkinesh)
paras: The fossil of Australopithecus afarensis is known as Lucy or Dinkinesh.
It was found in 1974 at Hadar, in the Afar region, Ethiopia.
Afarensis may have been an ancestor of the genus Homo.
